Typically, these counters track modifications to the underlying collection. If they differ, it indicates that the collection was structurally modified after the iterator was created, which makes the iterator's state inconsistent. The 'ConcurrentModificationException' is thrown to signal this error condition immediately, following the fail-fast behavior. The execution flow then terminates abnormally. The throw is unconditional once the condition is true, and no further code executes. The programmer intentionally throws this runtime exception to alert the caller that the iteration is no longer valid due to concurrent modification.
